A sclerenchyma cell is a plant cell with thick lignified walls, normally dead at maturity and specialized for structural strength. Includes fiber cells, that are greatly elongated; and sclereids, that are more isodiametric. Intermediate types exist. Cells may or may not be devoid of protoplasm at maturity. Cell form and size are variable.
search: go:0014001 go0014001 sclerenchyma cell differentiation

name: astrocyte development
definition: The process aimed at the progression of an astrocyte over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. An astrocyte is the most abundant type of glial cell. Astrocytes provide support for neurons and regulate the environment in which they function.
search: go:0014002 go0014002 astrocyte development

name: oligodendrocyte development
definition: The process aimed at the progression of an oligodendrocyte over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. An oligodendrocyte is a type of glial cell involved in myelinating the axons in the central nervous system.
search: go:0014003 go0014003 oligodendrocyte development

name: microglia differentiation
definition: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a microglial cell. Microglia are glial cells that act as the immune cells of the central nervous system. They form part of the supporting structure of this system.
search: go:0014004 go0014004 microglia differentiation

name: microglia development
definition: The process aimed at the progression of a microglial cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.
search: go:0014005 go0014005 microglia development

name: regulation of microglia differentiation
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of microglia differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a microglial cell.
search: go:0014006 go0014006 regulation of microglia differentiation

name: negative regulation of microglia differentiation
definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of microglia differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a microglial cell.
search: go:0014007 go0014007 negative regulation of microglia differentiation

name: positive regulation of microglia differentiation
definition: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of microglia differentiation, the process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a microglial cell.
search: go:0014008 go0014008 positive regulation of microglia differentiation

name: glial cell proliferation
definition: The multiplication or reproduction of glial cells by cell division, resulting in the expansion of their population. Glial cells exist throughout the nervous system, and include Schwann cells, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes among others.
search: go:0014009 go0014009 glial cell proliferation

name: Schwann cell proliferation
definition: The multiplication or reproduction of Schwann cells, resulting in the expansion of their population. Schwann cells are a type of glial cell in the peripheral nervous system.
search: go:0014010 go0014010 schwann cell proliferation

name: obsolete Schwann cell proliferation involved in axon regeneration
definition: OBSOLETE. The multiplication or reproduction of Schwann cells by cell division, resulting in the expansion of their population in response to an axonal lesion. The newly generated Schwann cells support subsequent axon regeneration in the peripheral nervous system.
search: go:0014011 go0014011 obsolete schwann cell proliferation involved in axon regeneration

name: peripheral nervous system axon regeneration
definition: The regrowth of axons outside the central nervous system (outside the brain and spinal cord) following an axonal injury.
search: go:0014012 go0014012 peripheral nervous system axon regeneration

name: regulation of gliogenesis
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of gliogenesis, the formation of mature glia.
search: go:0014013 go0014013 regulation of gliogenesis

name: negative regulation of gliogenesis
definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of gliogenesis, the formation of mature glia.
search: go:0014014 go0014014 negative regulation of gliogenesis

name: positive regulation of gliogenesis
definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of gliogenesis, the formation of mature glia.
search: go:0014015 go0014015 positive regulation of gliogenesis

name: neuroblast differentiation
definition: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neuroblast. There are at least four stages through which the pluripotent cells of epiblast or blastula become neuroblasts.
search: go:0014016 go0014016 neuroblast differentiation

name: neuroblast fate commitment
definition: The process in which the developmental fate of a cell becomes restricted such that it will differentiate into a neuroblast.
search: go:0014017 go0014017 neuroblast fate commitment

name: neuroblast fate specification
definition: The process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into a neuroblast in an environment that is neutral with respect to the developmental pathway. Upon specification, the cell fate can be reversed.
search: go:0014018 go0014018 neuroblast fate specification

name: neuroblast development
definition: The process aimed at the progression of a neuroblast over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific state, to the mature neuroblast. It does not include processes where the neuroblast turns into a glial cell or a neuron.
search: go:0014019 go0014019 neuroblast development

name: primary neural tube formation
definition: The formation of the neural tube from an epithelial cell sheet (the neuroepithelium or neural plate). In primary neurulation, the cells surrounding the neural plate direct the neural plate cells to proliferate, invaginate, and pinch off from the surface to form a hollow epithelial tube. Primary neurulation is the typical mechanism of formation of the anterior neural tube.
search: go:0014020 go0014020 primary neural tube formation

name: secondary neural tube formation
definition: The formation of the neural tube by coalescence of mesenchymal cells followed by their conversion to epithelial cells to form a solid cord that subsequently hollows out (cavitates) to create a hollow tube. Secondary neurulation is the typical mechanism of formation of the neural tube posterior to the posterior neuropore in mammals.
search: go:0014021 go0014021 secondary neural tube formation

name: neural plate elongation
definition: The process in which the neural plate is shaped by the intrinsic movement of the epidermal and neural plate regions.
search: go:0014022 go0014022 neural plate elongation

name: neural rod formation
definition: The formation of a solid rod of neurectoderm derived from the neural keel. The neural rod is roughly circular in cross section. Neural rod formation occurs during primary neurulation in teleosts.
search: go:0014023 go0014023 neural rod formation

name: neural keel formation
definition: The formation of a thickened region of the neurectoderm that is roughly triangular in cross section. The neural keel develops from the neural plate and develops into the neural rod. Neural keel formation occurs during primary neurulation in teleosts.
search: go:0014025 go0014025 neural keel formation

name: notochord formation
definition: The formation of the notochord from the chordamesoderm. The notochord is composed of large cells packed within a firm connective tissue sheath and is found in all chordates at the ventral surface of the neural tube. In vertebrates, the notochord contributes to the vertebral column.
search: go:0014028 go0014028 notochord formation

name: neural crest formation
definition: The formation of the specialized region of ectoderm between the neural ectoderm (neural plate) and non-neural ectoderm. The neural crest gives rise to the neural crest cells that migrate away from this region as neural tube formation proceeds.
search: go:0014029 go0014029 neural crest formation

name: mesenchymal cell fate commitment
definition: The process in which a cell becomes committed to become a mesenchymal cell.
search: go:0014030 go0014030 mesenchymal cell fate commitment

name: mesenchymal cell development
definition: The process aimed at the progression of a mesenchymal cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.
search: go:0014031 go0014031 mesenchymal cell development

name: neural crest cell development
definition: The process aimed at the progression of a neural crest cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to its specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell.
search: go:0014032 go0014032 neural crest cell development

name: neural crest cell differentiation
definition: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires specialized features of a neural crest cell.
search: go:0014033 go0014033 neural crest cell differentiation

name: neural crest cell fate commitment
definition: The process in which a cell becomes committed to become a neural crest cell.
search: go:0014034 go0014034 neural crest cell fate commitment

name: neural crest cell fate determination
definition: The process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into a neural crest cell regardless of its environment; upon determination, the cell fate cannot be reversed.
search: go:0014035 go0014035 neural crest cell fate determination

name: neural crest cell fate specification
definition: The process in which a cell becomes capable of differentiating autonomously into a neural crest cell in an environment that is neutral with respect to the developmental pathway; upon specification, the cell fate can be reversed.
search: go:0014036 go0014036 neural crest cell fate specification

name: Schwann cell differentiation
definition: The process in which a relatively unspecialized cell acquires the specialized features of a Schwann cell. Schwann cells are found in the peripheral nervous system, where they insulate neurons and axons, and regulate the environment in which neurons function.
search: go:0014037 go0014037 schwann cell differentiation

name: regulation of Schwann cell differentiation
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of Schwann cell differentiation.
search: go:0014038 go0014038 regulation of schwann cell differentiation

name: negative regulation of Schwann cell differentiation
definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of Schwann cell differentiation.
search: go:0014039 go0014039 negative regulation of schwann cell differentiation

name: positive regulation of Schwann cell differentiation
definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of Schwann cell differentiation.
search: go:0014040 go0014040 positive regulation of schwann cell differentiation

name: regulation of neuron maturation
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation, the process leading to the attainment of the full functional capacity of a neuron. This process is independent of morphogenetic change.
search: go:0014041 go0014041 regulation of neuron maturation

name: positive regulation of neuron maturation
definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation.
search: go:0014042 go0014042 positive regulation of neuron maturation

name: negative regulation of neuron maturation
definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of neuron maturation.
search: go:0014043 go0014043 negative regulation of neuron maturation

name: Schwann cell development
definition: The process aimed at the progression of a Schwann cell over time, from initial commitment of the cell to a specific fate, to the fully functional differentiated cell. Schwann cells are found in the peripheral nervous system, where they insulate neurons and axons, and regulate the environment in which neurons function.
search: go:0014044 go0014044 schwann cell development

name: establishment of endothelial blood-brain barrier
definition: Establishment of the endothelial barrier between the blood and the brain. The endothelial cells in the brain capillaries are packed tightly together preventing the passage of most molecules from the blood into the brain. Only lipid soluble molecules or those that are actively transported can pass through the blood-brain barrier.
search: go:0014045 go0014045 establishment of endothelial blood-brain barrier

name: dopamine secretion
definition: The regulated release of dopamine by a cell. Dopamine is a catecholamine and a precursor of adrenaline and noradrenaline. It acts as a neurotransmitter in the central nervous system but it is also produced peripherally and acts as a hormone.
search: go:0014046 go0014046 dopamine secretion

name: glutamate secretion
definition: The controlled release of glutamate by a cell. The glutamate is the most abundant excitatory neurotransmitter in the nervous system.
search: go:0014047 go0014047 glutamate secretion

name: regulation of glutamate secretion
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate.
search: go:0014048 go0014048 regulation of glutamate secretion

name: positive regulation of glutamate secretion
definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate.
search: go:0014049 go0014049 positive regulation of glutamate secretion

name: negative regulation of glutamate secretion
definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the controlled release of glutamate.
search: go:0014050 go0014050 negative regulation of glutamate secretion

name: gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion
definition: The regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid by a cell or a tissue. The gamma-aminobutyric acid is the principal inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain but is also found in several extraneural tissues.
search: go:0014051 go0014051 gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion

name: regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid.
search: go:0014052 go0014052 regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion

name: negative regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion
definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid.
search: go:0014053 go0014053 negative regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion

name: positive regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion
definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of gamma-aminobutyric acid.
search: go:0014054 go0014054 positive regulation of gamma-aminobutyric acid secretion

name: acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission
definition: The regulated release of acetylcholine by a cell. The acetylcholine acts as a neurotransmitter that acts in both the peripheral nervous system (PNS) and central nervous system (CNS).
search: go:0014055 go0014055 acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission

name: regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of acetylcholine.
search: go:0014056 go0014056 regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission

name: positive regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission
definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of acetylcholine.
search: go:0014057 go0014057 positive regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission

name: negative regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission
definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of acetylcholine.
search: go:0014058 go0014058 negative regulation of acetylcholine secretion, neurotransmission

name: regulation of dopamine secretion
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of dopamine.
search: go:0014059 go0014059 regulation of dopamine secretion

name: regulation of epinephrine secretion
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of epinephrine.
search: go:0014060 go0014060 regulation of epinephrine secretion

name: regulation of norepinephrine secretion
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of norepinephrine.
search: go:0014061 go0014061 regulation of norepinephrine secretion

name: regulation of serotonin secretion
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of serotonin.
search: go:0014062 go0014062 regulation of serotonin secretion

definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of serotonin.
search: go:0014063 go0014063 negative regulation of serotonin secretion

name: positive regulation of serotonin secretion
definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of serotonin.
search: go:0014064 go0014064 positive regulation of serotonin secretion

name: obsolete phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase signaling
definition: OBSOLETE. A series of reactions within the signal-receiving cell, mediated by the intracellular phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K). Many cell surface receptor linked signaling pathways signal through PI3K to regulate numerous cellular functions.
search: go:0014065 go0014065 obsolete phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase signaling

name: obsolete regulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase signaling
definition: OBSOLETE. Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of signal transduction mediated by the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase cascade.
search: go:0014066 go0014066 obsolete regulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase signaling

name: obsolete negative regulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase signaling
definition: OBSOLETE. Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of signal transduction mediated by the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase cascade.
search: go:0014067 go0014067 obsolete negative regulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase signaling

name: obsolete positive regulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase signaling
definition: OBSOLETE. Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of signal transduction mediated by the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase cascade.
search: go:0014068 go0014068 obsolete positive regulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase signaling

name: postsynaptic density
definition: An electron dense network of proteins within and adjacent to the postsynaptic membrane of an asymmetric, neuron-neuron synapse. Its major components include neurotransmitter receptors and the proteins that spatially and functionally organize them such as anchoring and scaffolding molecules, signaling enzymes and cytoskeletal components.
search: go:0014069 go0014069 postsynaptic density

name: obsolete response to organic cyclic compound
definition: OBSOLETE. Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an organic cyclic compound stimulus.
search: go:0014070 go0014070 obsolete response to organic cyclic compound

name: response to cycloalkane
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a cycloalkane stimulus. A cycloalkane is a cyclic saturated hydrocarbon having the general formula CnH2n.
search: go:0014071 go0014071 response to cycloalkane

name: response to isoquinoline alkaloid
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an isoquinoline alkaloid stimulus. An isoquinoline alkaloid is any member of a group of compounds with the heterocyclic ring structure of benzo(c)pyridine which is a structure characteristic of the group of opium alkaloids.
search: go:0014072 go0014072 response to isoquinoline alkaloid

name: response to tropane
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a tropane stimulus. Tropane is a nitrogenous bicyclic organic compound mainly known for a group of alkaloids derived from it (called tropane alkaloids), which include, among others, atropine and cocaine.
search: go:0014073 go0014073 response to tropane

name: response to purine-containing compound
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a purine-containing compound stimulus.
search: go:0014074 go0014074 response to purine-containing compound

name: response to amine
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an amine stimulus. An amine is a compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by hydrocarbyl groups.
search: go:0014075 go0014075 response to amine

name: response to fluoxetine
definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a fluoxetine stimulus. Fluoxetine increases the extracellular level of the neurotransmitter serotonin by inhibiting its reuptake into the presynaptic cell, increasing the level of serotonin available to bind to the postsynaptic receptor.
search: go:0014076 go0014076 response to fluoxetine

name: junctional sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane
definition: The part of the sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane that contains calcium release channels, is devoted to calcium release and is juxtaposed to transverse tubule membrane. The junctional sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane consists of the junctional region of the terminal cisterna membrane.
search: go:0014701 go0014701 junctional sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane

name: free sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane
definition: The part of the sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane that contains calcium pumps and is devoted to calcium uptake. The free sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane consists of the longitudinal sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane and the non-junctional region of the terminal cisterna membrane.
search: go:0014702 go0014702 free sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane

name: oscillatory muscle contraction
definition: A process in which force is generated within oscillatory skeletal muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. Oscillatory muscle contraction occurs in insect wing muscles and is characterized by asynchrony between action potential and contraction and by stretch activation.
search: go:0014703 go0014703 oscillatory muscle contraction

name: intercalated disc
definition: A complex cell-cell junction at which myofibrils terminate in cardiomyocytes; mediates mechanical and electrochemical integration between individual cardiomyocytes. The intercalated disc contains regions of tight mechanical attachment (fasciae adherentes and desmosomes) and electrical coupling (gap junctions) between adjacent cells.
search: go:0014704 go0014704 intercalated disc

name: C zone
definition: A region of the A band in which myosin-binding protein C is located and that can be seen by electron microscopy. This is a functional zone that also includes myosin.

name: striated muscle tissue development
definition: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a striated muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Striated muscle contain fibers that are divided by transverse bands into striations, and cardiac and skeletal muscle are types of striated muscle. Skeletal muscle myoblasts fuse to form myotubes and eventually multinucleated muscle fibers. The fusion of cardiac cells is very rare and can only form binucleate cells.
search: go:0014706 go0014706 striated muscle tissue development

name: branchiomeric skeletal muscle development
definition: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The branchiomeric muscle is derived from cranial mesoderm and controls facial expression, pharyngeal and laryngeal function, operating the jaw. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle. Branchiomeric muscles of mammals correspond to the gill musculature of fish.
search: go:0014707 go0014707 branchiomeric skeletal muscle development

name: regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of somitomeric trunk muscle development.
search: go:0014708 go0014708 regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development

name: positive regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development
definition: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of somitomeric trunk muscle development. The somitomeric trunk muscle is derived from somitomeric mesoderm. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle.
search: go:0014709 go0014709 positive regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development

name: negative regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development
definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of somitomeric trunk muscle development. The somitomeric trunk muscle is derived from somitomeric mesoderm. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle.
search: go:0014710 go0014710 negative regulation of somitomeric trunk muscle development

name: regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development. Branchiomeric skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure.
search: go:0014711 go0014711 regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development

name: positive regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development
definition: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development. Branchiomeric skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure.
search: go:0014712 go0014712 positive regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development

name: negative regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development
definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development. Branchiomeric skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the branchiomeric skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure.
search: go:0014713 go0014713 negative regulation of branchiomeric skeletal muscle development

name: myoblast fate commitment in head
definition: The process, taking place in the head, whereby the developmental fate of a cell becomes restricted such that it will develop into a myoblast. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers.
search: go:0014714 go0014714 myoblast fate commitment in head

name: myoblast fate commitment in trunk
definition: The process taking place in the trunk whereby the developmental fate of a cell becomes restricted such that it will develop into a myoblast. A myoblast is a mononucleate cell type that, by fusion with other myoblasts, gives rise to the myotubes that eventually develop into skeletal muscle fibers.
search: go:0014715 go0014715 myoblast fate commitment in trunk

name: obsolete skeletal muscle satellite stem cell asymmetric division involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
definition: OBSOLETE. Skeletal muscle satellite cell asymmetric division that occurs during a process in which damaged muscle tissue is being rebuilt.
search: go:0014716 go0014716 obsolete skeletal muscle satellite stem cell asymmetric division involved in skeletal muscle regeneration

name: regulation of satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of satellite cell activation. The satellite cell activation is the process that initiates satellite cell division by causing it to move from quiescence to the G1 stage of the cell cycle. The cell swells and there are a number of other small changes. The cells then start to divide. Following cell division the cells will differentiate.
search: go:0014717 go0014717 regulation of satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration

name: positive regulation of satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration
definition: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of activation of satellite cell involved in skeletal muscle regeneration. The activation of satellite cell is the process that initiates satellite cell division by causing it to move from quiescence to the G1 stage of the cell cycle. The cell swells and there are a number of other small changes. The cells then start to divide. Following cell division the cells will differentiate.
search: go:0014718 go0014718 positive regulation of satellite cell activation involved in skeletal muscle regeneration

name: skeletal muscle satellite cell activation
definition: The change of a skeletal muscle satellite cell from a mitotically quiescent to a mitotically active state following exposure to some activating factor such as a cellular or soluble ligand. In adult muscle, satellite cells become activated to divide and differentiate in response to muscle damage.
search: go:0014719 go0014719 skeletal muscle satellite cell activation

name: tonic skeletal muscle contraction
definition: A process in which force is generated within tonic skeletal muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The tonic skeletal muscle is characterized by long lasting contractile responses and high resistance to fatigue.
search: go:0014720 go0014720 tonic skeletal muscle contraction

name: twitch skeletal muscle contraction
definition: A process in which force is generated within twitch skeletal muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. The twitch skeletal muscle responds to neurostimulations with a contraction followed by a relaxation.
search: go:0014721 go0014721 twitch skeletal muscle contraction

name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by calcium ion signaling
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction by changing the calcium ion signals that trigger contraction.
search: go:0014722 go0014722 regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by calcium ion signaling

name: regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by modulation of calcium ion sensitivity of myofibril
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of skeletal muscle contraction by changing calcium ion binding affinity of the myofibril.
search: go:0014723 go0014723 regulation of skeletal muscle contraction by modulation of calcium ion sensitivity of myofibril

name: regulation of twitch skeletal muscle contraction
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of twitch skeletal muscle contraction.
search: go:0014724 go0014724 regulation of twitch skeletal muscle contraction

name: regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of extraocular skeletal muscle development. Extraocular skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the extraocular skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The extraocular muscle is derived from cranial mesoderm and controls eye movements. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle.
search: go:0014725 go0014725 regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development

name: negative regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development
definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of extraocular skeletal muscle development. Extraocular skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the extraocular skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The extraocular muscle is derived from cranial mesoderm and controls eye movements. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle.
search: go:0014726 go0014726 negative regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development

name: positive regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development
definition: Any process that activates, maintains or increases the frequency, rate or extent of extraocular skeletal muscle development. Extraocular skeletal muscle development is the process whose specific outcome is the progression of the extraocular skeletal muscle over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The extraocular muscle is derived from cranial mesoderm and controls eye movements. The muscle begins its development with the differentiation of the muscle cells and ends with the mature muscle.
search: go:0014727 go0014727 positive regulation of extraocular skeletal muscle development

name: regulation of the force of skeletal muscle contraction
definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the force of skeletal muscle contraction. The force of skeletal muscle contraction is produced by acto-myosin interaction processes through the formation of cross bridges.
search: go:0014728 go0014728 regulation of the force of skeletal muscle contraction

name: regulation of the velocity of shortening of skeletal muscle modulating contraction
definition: Any process that modulates velocity of shortening of a skeletal muscle contraction. The shortening leads to reduction of the length of muscle fibers and sarcomeres.
search: go:0014729 go0014729 regulation of the velocity of shortening of skeletal muscle modulating contraction

name: skeletal muscle regeneration at neuromuscular junction
definition: The regrowth of muscle tissue to repair injured or damaged muscle fibers in the postnatal stage at the neuromuscular junction. Regeneration of neuromuscular junctions occurs in an orderly way and relies on communication between nerve and muscle. Skeletal myofibers regenerate after injury and form neuro-muscular junctions with motor axons similar to normal ones. Regenerating myofibers develop within the basal lamina sheaths (satellite cells) of original myofibers.
search: go:0014730 go0014730 skeletal muscle regeneration at neuromuscular junction

name: spectrin-associated cytoskeleton
definition: The part of the cytoskeleton composed of spectrin, protein 4.1 and ankyrin. Spectrin-associated cytoskeleton is associated with the plasma membrane.
search: go:0014731 go0014731 spectrin-associated cytoskeleton

name: skeletal muscle atrophy
definition: A process, occurring in skeletal muscle, that is characterized by a decrease in protein content, fiber diameter, force production and fatigue resistance in response to different conditions such as starvation, aging and disuse.
search: go:0014732 go0014732 skeletal muscle atrophy

name: regulation of skeletal muscle adaptation
definition: Any process in which skeletal muscle adapts, with consequent modifications to structural and/or functional phenotypes, in response to a stimulus. Stimuli include contractile activity, loading conditions, substrate supply, and environmental factors. These adaptive events occur in both muscle fibers and associated structures (motoneurons and capillaries), and they involve alterations in regulatory mechanisms, contractile properties and metabolic capacities.
search: go:0014733 go0014733 regulation of skeletal muscle adaptation

name: skeletal muscle hypertrophy
definition: The enlargement or overgrowth of all or part of an organ due to an increase in size (not length) of individual muscle fibers without cell division. In the case of skeletal muscle cells this happens due to the additional synthesis of sarcomeric proteins and assembly of myofibrils.

Others, however, catalyze elimination of another component, e.g. water, which is followed by spontaneous reactions that lead to breakage of the C-N bond, e.g. L-serine ammonia-lyase (EC:4.3.1.17), so that the overall reaction is C(-OH)-CH(-NH2) = CH2-CO- + NH4+, i.e. an elimination with rearrangement. name: obsolete DNA replication accessory factor
definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).

name: viral nucleocapsid
definition: The complete protein-nucleic acid complex that is the packaged form of the genome in a virus particle.
search: go:0019013 go0019013 viral nucleocapsid

name: obsolete viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. The whole of the genetic information of a virus, contained as either DNA or RNA.
search: go:0019015 go0019015 obsolete viral genome

name: obsolete non-segmented viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A viral genome that consists of one continuous nucleic acid molecule.
search: go:0019016 go0019016 obsolete non-segmented viral genome

name: obsolete segmented viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A viral genome that is divided into two or more physically separate molecules of nucleic acid and packaged into a single virion.
search: go:0019017 go0019017 obsolete segmented viral genome

name: obsolete bipartite viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A segmented viral genome consisting of two sub-genomic nucleic acids but each nucleic acid is packaged into a different virion.
search: go:0019018 go0019018 obsolete bipartite viral genome

name: obsolete tripartite viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A segmented viral genome consisting of three sub-genomic nucleic acids but each nucleic acid is packaged into a different virion.
search: go:0019019 go0019019 obsolete tripartite viral genome

name: obsolete multipartite viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A segmented viral genome consisting of more than three sub-genomic nucleic acids but each nucleic acid is packaged into a different virion.
search: go:0019020 go0019020 obsolete multipartite viral genome

name: obsolete DNA viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A viral genome composed of deoxyribonucleic acid.
search: go:0019021 go0019021 obsolete dna viral genome

name: obsolete RNA viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A viral genome composed of ribonucleic acid. This results in genome replication and expression of genetic information being inextricably linked.
search: go:0019022 go0019022 obsolete rna viral genome

name: obsolete dsRNA viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A viral genome composed of double stranded RNA.
search: go:0019023 go0019023 obsolete dsrna viral genome

name: obsolete ssRNA viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A viral genome composed of single stranded RNA of either positive or negative sense.
search: go:0019024 go0019024 obsolete ssrna viral genome

name: obsolete positive sense viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A single stranded RNA genome with the same nucleotide polarity as mRNA.
search: go:0019025 go0019025 obsolete positive sense viral genome

name: obsolete negative sense viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A single stranded RNA genome with the opposite nucleotide polarity as mRNA.
search: go:0019026 go0019026 obsolete negative sense viral genome

name: obsolete ambisense viral genome
definition: OBSOLETE. A RNA genome that contains coding regions that are either positive sense or negative sense on the same RNA molecule.
search: go:0019027 go0019027 obsolete ambisense viral genome

name: viral capsid
definition: The protein coat that surrounds the infective nucleic acid in some virus particles. It comprises numerous regularly arranged subunits, or capsomeres.
search: go:0019028 go0019028 viral capsid

name: helical viral capsid
definition: The protein coat that surrounds the infective nucleic acid in some virus particles; the subunits are arranged to form a protein helix with the genetic material contained within. Tobacco mosaic virus has such a capsid structure.
search: go:0019029 go0019029 helical viral capsid

name: icosahedral viral capsid
definition: The protein coat that surrounds the infective nucleic acid in some virus particles; the subunits are arranged to form an icosahedron, a solid with 20 faces and 12 vertices. Icosahedral capsids have 12 pentamers plus 10(T-1) hexamers, where T is the triangulation number. Tobacco satellite necrosis virus has such a capsid structure.
search: go:0019030 go0019030 icosahedral viral capsid

name: viral envelope
definition: The lipid bilayer of a virion that surrounds the protein capsid. May also contain glycoproteins.
search: go:0019031 go0019031 viral envelope

name: obsolete viral glycoprotein
definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).
search: go:0019032 go0019032 obsolete viral glycoprotein

name: viral tegument
definition: A structure lying between the capsid and envelope of a virus, varying in thickness and often distributed asymmetrically.
search: go:0019033 go0019033 viral tegument

name: viral replication complex
definition: Specific locations and structures in the virus infected cell involved in replicating the viral genome.
search: go:0019034 go0019034 viral replication complex

name: viral integration complex
definition: A nucleoprotein complex containing viral genetic material and the viral integrase, required for genome integration into the host's genome. May contain other proteins.
search: go:0019035 go0019035 viral integration complex

name: viral transcriptional complex
definition: Specific locations and structures in the virus infected cell involved in transcribing the viral genome.
search: go:0019036 go0019036 viral transcriptional complex

name: obsolete viral assembly intermediate
definition: OBSOLETE. Specific locations and structures in the virus infected cell involved in assembling new virions.
search: go:0019037 go0019037 obsolete viral assembly intermediate

name: obsolete provirus
definition: OBSOLETE. The name given to a viral genome after it has been integrated into the host genome; particularly applies to retroviruses and is a required part of the retroviral replication cycle.
search: go:0019038 go0019038 obsolete provirus

name: obsolete viral-cell fusion molecule activity
definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).
search: go:0019039 go0019039 obsolete viral-cell fusion molecule activity

name: obsolete viral host shutoff protein
definition: OBSOLETE. (Was not defined before being made obsolete).
search: go:0019040 go0019040 obsolete viral host shutoff protein

name: viral latency
definition: The process by which, after initial infection, a virus lies dormant within a cell and viral production ceases. The process ends when the virus switches from latency and starts to replicate.
search: go:0019042 go0019042 viral latency

name: establishment of viral latency
definition: A process by which a virus establishes a latent state within its host, either as an integrated provirus within the host genome or as an episome, where viral genome remains in the cytoplasm or nucleus as distinct objects.
search: go:0019043 go0019043 establishment of viral latency

name: maintenance of viral latency
definition: The perpetuation of a latent state, generally by repressing the viruses own lytic genes expression and ensuring expression of viral genes which function to keep the viral genome from being detected by the host defense mechanisms.
search: go:0019044 go0019044 maintenance of viral latency

name: latent virus replication
definition: Any process required for latent viral replication in a cell.
search: go:0019045 go0019045 latent virus replication

name: release from viral latency
definition: The process by which a virus begins to replicate following a latency replication decision (switch).
search: go:0019046 go0019046 release from viral latency

name: obsolete modulation by virus of host process
definition: OBSOLETE. The process in which a virus effects a change in the structure or processes of its host organism.
search: go:0019048 go0019048 obsolete modulation by virus of host process

name: obsolete virus-mediated perturbation of host defense response
definition: OBSOLETE. A process in which a virus interferes with the ability of the host to mount a defense in response to its presence. Host defenses may be induced by the presence of the virus or may be preformed (e.g. physical barriers). The host is defined as the larger of the organisms involved in a symbiotic interaction.
search: go:0019049 go0019049 obsolete virus-mediated perturbation of host defense response

name: obsolete suppression by virus of host apoptotic process
definition: OBSOLETE. A process in which a virus gene product suppresses host apoptosis, leading to a decrease in the frequency, rate or extent of apoptosis in the host cell.
search: go:0019050 go0019050 obsolete suppression by virus of host apoptotic process

name: obsolete induction by virus of host apoptotic process
definition: OBSOLETE. A process in which a viral gene product activates host apoptosis, leading to an increase in the frequency, rate or extent of apoptosis in the host cell.
search: go:0019051 go0019051 obsolete induction by virus of host apoptotic process

name: obsolete modulation by virus of host cellular process
definition: OBSOLETE. The process in which a virus effects a change in the processes and activities of its host organism.
search: go:0019054 go0019054 obsolete modulation by virus of host cellular process

name: obsolete perturbation by virus of host cell cycle regulation
definition: OBSOLETE. Interactions, directly with the host cell macromolecular machinery, to allow a virus to modulate the rate of the host cell cycle to facilitate virus replication.
search: go:0019055 go0019055 obsolete perturbation by virus of host cell cycle regulation

name: obsolete modulation by virus of host transcription
definition: OBSOLETE. Any process in which a virus modulates the frequency, rate or extent of its host's transcription.
search: go:0019056 go0019056 obsolete modulation by virus of host transcription

name: symbiont-mediated perturbation of host translation
definition: A process in which a symbiont alters or subverts translation of mRNA into protein in its host. The host is defined as the larger of the organisms involved in a symbiotic interaction.
search: go:0019057 go0019057 symbiont-mediated perturbation of host translation

name: viral life cycle
definition: A set of processes which all viruses follow to ensure survival; includes attachment and entry of the virus particle, decoding of genome information, translation of viral mRNA by host ribosomes, genome replication, and assembly and release of viral particles containing the genome.
search: go:0019058 go0019058 viral life cycle

name: obsolete initiation of viral infection
definition: OBSOLETE. The set of processes involved in the start of virus infection of cells.
search: go:0019059 go0019059 obsolete initiation of viral infection

name: intracellular transport of viral protein in host cell
definition: The directed movement of a viral protein within the host cell.
search: go:0019060 go0019060 intracellular transport of viral protein in host cell

name: uncoating of virus
definition: The process by which an incoming virus is disassembled in the host cell to release a replication-competent viral genome.
search: go:0019061 go0019061 uncoating of virus

name: virion attachment to host cell
definition: The process by which a virion protein binds to molecules on the host cellular surface or host cell surface projection.
search: go:0019062 go0019062 virion attachment to host cell

name: fusion of virus membrane with host plasma membrane
definition: Fusion of a viral membrane with the host cell membrane during viral entry. Results in release of the virion contents into the cytoplasm.
search: go:0019064 go0019064 fusion of virus membrane with host plasma membrane

name: receptor-mediated endocytosis of virus by host cell
definition: Any receptor-mediated endocytosis that is involved in the uptake of a virus into a host cell; successive instances of virus endocytosis result in the accumulation of virus particles within the cell.
search: go:0019065 go0019065 receptor-mediated endocytosis of virus by host cell

name: obsolete translocation of virus into host cell
definition: OBSOLETE. The translocation of an entire virus particle across the host cell plasma membrane.
search: go:0019066 go0019066 obsolete translocation of virus into host cell

name: virion assembly
definition: A late phase of the viral life cycle during which all the components necessary for the formation of a mature virion collect at a particular site in the cell and the basic structure of the virus particle is formed.
search: go:0019068 go0019068 virion assembly

name: viral capsid assembly
definition: The assembly of a virus capsid from its protein subunits.
search: go:0019069 go0019069 viral capsid assembly

name: viral genome maturation
definition: The processes involved in creating a mature, stable viral genome. Begins after genome replication with a newly synthesized nucleic acid and ends when the genome is ready to be packaged. Includes the addition of proteins to the newly synthesized genome, and DNA repair processes.
search: go:0019070 go0019070 viral genome maturation

name: obsolete viral DNA cleavage involved in viral genome maturation
definition: OBSOLETE. The cleavage of viral DNA into singular functional units.
search: go:0019071 go0019071 obsolete viral dna cleavage involved in viral genome maturation

name: viral genome packaging
definition: The encapsulation of the viral genome within the capsid.
search: go:0019072 go0019072 viral genome packaging

name: viral DNA genome packaging
definition: The packing of viral DNA into a capsid.
search: go:0019073 go0019073 viral dna genome packaging

name: viral RNA genome packaging
definition: The packaging of viral RNA (single-stranded or double-stranded) into a nucleocapsid.
search: go:0019074 go0019074 viral rna genome packaging

name: virus maturation
definition: The refolding and structural rearrangements of virion parts to transition from the intermediate virion to the more mature virion. Maturation usually involves proteolysis events and changes in the folding of the virion proteins. Can occur inside the host cell or after release.
search: go:0019075 go0019075 virus maturation

name: viral release from host cell
definition: The dissemination of mature viral particles from a host cell, e.g. by cell lysis or the budding of virus particles from the cell membrane.
search: go:0019076 go0019076 viral release from host cell

name: obsolete lytic viral budding
definition: OBSOLETE. A form of viral release in which the viral particles bud out through cellular membranes, resulting in cell lysis. It is also a form of viral envelopment.
search: go:0019078 go0019078 obsolete lytic viral budding

name: viral genome replication
definition: Any process involved directly in viral genome replication, including viral nucleotide metabolism.
search: go:0019079 go0019079 viral genome replication

name: viral gene expression
definition: A process by which a viral gene is converted into a mature gene product or products (proteins or RNA). This includes viral transcription, processing to produce a mature RNA product, and viral translation.
search: go:0019080 go0019080 viral gene expression

name: viral translation
definition: A process by which viral mRNA is translated into viral protein, using the host cellular machinery.
search: go:0019081 go0019081 viral translation

name: viral protein processing
definition: Any protein maturation process achieved by the cleavage of a peptide bond or bonds within a viral protein.
search: go:0019082 go0019082 viral protein processing

name: viral transcription
definition: The process by which a viral genome, or part of a viral genome, is transcribed within the host cell.
search: go:0019083 go0019083 viral transcription

name: middle viral transcription
definition: The viral transcription that takes place after early transcription in the viral life cycle, and which involves the transcription of genes required for replication.
search: go:0019084 go0019084 middle viral transcription

name: early viral transcription
definition: The first phase of viral transcription that occurs after entry of the virus into the host cell, but prior to viral genome replication. It involves the transcription of genes for non-structural proteins, and for lytic viruses, the early gene products are involved in establishing control over the host cell.
search: go:0019085 go0019085 early viral transcription

name: late viral transcription
definition: The transcription of the final group of viral genes of the viral life cycle, following middle transcription, or where middle transcription doesn't occur, following early transcription. Involves the transcription of genes encoding structural proteins.
search: go:0019086 go0019086 late viral transcription

name: symbiont-mediated transformation of host cell
definition: A symbiont-induced cellular transformation resulting in immortalized cells, or cells capable of indefinite replication. Usually mediated by viruses.
search: go:0019087 go0019087 symbiont-mediated transformation of host cell

name: obsolete transmission of virus
definition: OBSOLETE. The transfer of virions in order to create new infection.
search: go:0019089 go0019089 obsolete transmission of virus

search: go:0019092 go0019092 mitochondrial srrna export from mitochondrion

name: pole plasm mitochondrial lrRNA localization
definition: Any process in which mitochondrial large ribosomal RNA is transported to, or maintained in, the oocyte pole plasm. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.
search: go:0019096 go0019096 pole plasm mitochondrial lrrna localization

name: pole plasm mitochondrial srRNA localization
definition: Any process in which mitochondrial small ribosomal RNA is transported to, or maintained in, the oocyte pole plasm. An example of this is found in Drosophila melanogaster.
search: go:0019097 go0019097 pole plasm mitochondrial srrna localization

Only the M and S subunits are required for this reaction. If the complex binds to an unmethylated recognition site, then the complex translocates the DNA bidirectionally in an ATP-dependent manner. When the translocation is stalled by impact with another complex or unusual DNA structure, the enzyme functions as an endonuclease and cleavage of the DNA will occur, hundreds or thousands of base pairs away from the recognition site. These DNA restriction systems are used by bacteria to defend against phage and other foreign DNA that may enter a cell.

Cleavage occurs at a specific distance away from one of the recognition sites. The Mod subunit can act alone as a methyltansferase. DNA restriction systems such as this are used by bacteria to defend against phage and other foreign DNA that may enter a cell.
